qs.ours: Πεπραγμενον αὐτῳ, without the preposition. Though somewhat uncommon, instances of this occur in Greek; and it is much more natural to understand it thus here, than to suppose that the passing of a capital sentence, or anything done by Herod to Christ, should be called a thing deserving death on Christ's part. Polybius says Hermiad finished his life in this way, undergoing a punishment by no means equal to the things done by him, that is, as his crimes deserved, οὐδεμιαν ὑποσχων τιμωριαν ἀξιαν των αὐτῳ πεπραγμενων. And Josephus, at the end of his life, written by himself, says, "These are the things done by me during (or the actions of) my whole life: Ταυτα μεν τα πεπραγμενα μοι δια παντος του βιου ἐστιν.
